- Wet, dark, slimy rotting tissue
- Soft brown/tan decomposed tissue at the lower node
- Surrounding leaves wilted and yellowing

**Reference comparison:**
- **Bacterial_Stalk_Rot**: References 42 and 51 showed whole-plant wilting; reference 16 showed brown leaf sheaths. The wet slimy tissue in the test image is most characteristic of bacterial infection
- **Charcoal_Stalk_Rot**: Internal dry charcoal-black discoloration - doesn't match
- **Diplodia_Stalk_Rot**: Dry tan stalk - doesn't match
- **Physoderma_Stalk_Rot**: Purple-black discrete spots on sheath - doesn't match
- **Common_Smut**: Dark gall structures - doesn't match
- All leaf diseases (Northern Leaf Blight, Gray Leaf Spot, Common Rust, Tar Spot, Goss's Wilt) - clearly wrong, different anatomy

The wet, dark, mushy crown rot with slimy exudate is the hallmark of Bacterial Stalk Rot. No other candidate comes close visually.
